representable_set.encoding: GF-T16 magnitude = (offset << 9) | mantissa; the word is (sign << 16) | magnitude
representable_set.offset_ceiling_source: specs/ternary/gft_axpy.t27, the magmul saturation `if (res >= 80)` -- read, not hardcoded

identity_is_partial.claim: smul(x, ONE) == x holds on the whole representable set except negative zero, and fails on every word outside it
identity_is_partial.method: exhaustive over all 131072 words (65536 magnitudes x both signs), partitioned by representability

the_one_exception.why: sign-magnitude admits two zeros. smul's guard tests the whole word (a == 0), so negative zero passes it; magmul then returns 0 and the mag==0 guard normalises the result to +0. Identity fails, and correctly so -- the operator is collapsing a redundant encoding.

identity_is_partial.why: magmul saturates out_off at the ceiling, so an out-of-range operand comes back clamped. This is the specified behaviour, not a defect.

commutativity_is_total.method: 2359296 pairs: every one of 65536 magnitudes crossed with 9 representative magnitudes, both sign combinations, both operand orders; plus symmetry by inspection of magmul (prod, sm and the sign xor are each symmetric)

consequence: An on-die identity clause driven by a free-running counter has an EXPIRY DATE. Past it the clause is false for the right reason and the sticky latch records it as a defect forever.

sharpest.gft_sadd_sweep_jtag.v: liveA valid for 3 min, liveB for 23 s -- this wrapper's clauses expire while the operator is still being loaded
sharpest.gft_xorpercep_jtag.v: lfsr is NEVER valid: a 32-bit LFSR seeded 0x1ACE5EED is outside the representable set from the first cycle

does_it_explain_the_open_failure: NO. gft_smul's live counter is valid for 20992 beats (~12 h nominal) and the die was read within minutes. This is a LATENT trap the instrument found, not the cause of the measured COMM/IND failure.
